---
title: "Colorado Net Migration by Age"
subtitle: "2010-2020 and 2020-2025"
---

The Census Bureau publishes county population by age, and it publishes total net
migration by county, but not net migration *by age* below the state level. This
site estimates it as a demographic residual: for each cohort, net migration is
whatever is left once observed births and deaths are removed from the population
change.

$$
\text{NM}(c) = \text{Pop}_{\text{end}}(c) - \text{Pop}_{\text{start}}(c) - \text{Births}(c) + \text{Deaths}(c)
$$

Cohorts are keyed by **age at the end of the period**, so a group labelled 25–29
in the 2010–2020 period is the people who were 25–29 in 2020 and 15–19 in 2010.
Keying on the ending age means every group has a real age, including the children
born along the way.

## The headline

Colorado's net migration fell from about **45,000 a year** in 2010–2020 to about
**28,300 a year** in 2020–2025. The age profile changed more than the total did.

| Age at end of period | 2010–2020 | 2020–2025 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 5–9 | 8.3 | 4.3 |
| 10–14 | 9.5 | 2.0 |
| **25–29** | **26.9** | **36.3** |
| 30–34 | 27.6 | 19.3 |
| 45–49 | 3.2 | −1.3 |
| 60–64 | −0.2 | −5.9 |
| 65–69 | 0.5 | −6.0 |

: Annual net migration per 1,000 people {.striped tbl-colwidths="[40,30,30]"}

The peak did not just shrink — it moved, narrowed, and grew taller. Colorado used
to draw people across a broad plateau of young adulthood, with 25–29 and 30–34
gaining at almost the same rate. That plateau has collapsed into a single sharp
peak at 25–29, now the highest rate in either period.

Either side of it, rates fell almost everywhere. The inflow of school-age
children largely stopped, and every group from 45–49 upward crossed into negative
territory. Colorado is drawing twenty-somethings harder than it ever did, and is
no longer drawing the families and older movers that used to come with them.

## Caveat

The Census and SDO county age estimates are themselves cohort-component output,
built from these same vital records plus the agencies' own migration signals.
This recovers the net migration by age *implied by* those published estimates. It
is the right number for anyone working from them, but it inherits their
assumptions rather than testing them.
